content.text:
I checked current online laptop deal roundups and retailer pages. **If you can wait, the biggest near-term sale is Amazon Prime Day 2026, June 23–26**, with Amazon saying select **Asus and HP laptops** will be up to **40% off**. So unless you need a laptop immediately, I’d wait ~2 weeks and compare Prime Day prices against Best Buy, Lenovo, Dell, and Costco. ([androidcentral.com](https://www.androidcentral.com/streaming-tv/amazon/amazon-prime-day-2026-announced))

## Best laptop deals to consider right now

| Best for | Deal | Why it looks good |
|---|---:|---|
| **Best budget Windows pick** | **Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5 Ryzen AI 5 340 16" — $599.99** with promo code `IDEASUMMERUS` | Stronger long-term buy than ultra-cheap unknown-brand laptops; 16" size, modern Ryzen AI chip, $350 off list per DealNews. ([dealnews.com](https://www.dealnews.com/c49/Computers/Laptops/)) |
| **Best Apple value** | **13" MacBook Air M5, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD — about $949** | Great all-around laptop if you want macOS, battery life, and resale value; MacRumors shows multiple configurations discounted vs. Apple list pricing. ([macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/guide/macbook-pro-air-deals/)) |
| **Best bigger MacBook deal** | **15" MacBook Air M5, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD — about $1,099–$1,149** | Better if you want a larger screen but don’t need MacBook Pro performance. ([macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/guide/macbook-pro-air-deals/)) |
| **Best cheap daily-use Windows laptop** | **Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3x — $599.99** | PCWorld highlighted it as a strong budget pick with 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD, and long battery life; good for students/office/web use. ([pcworld.com](https://www.pcworld.com/article/3145503/best-memorial-day-laptop-deals.html)) |
| **Best gaming deal mentioned** | **Alienware 16 Aurora — $1,069.97** | PCWorld listed it as its best gaming-laptop deal, marked $490 off. Good if you need GPU performance. ([pcworld.com](https://www.pcworld.com/article/3145503/best-memorial-day-laptop-deals.html)) |
| **Best premium performance deal** | **Lenovo Legion Pro 7i — $2,599.99** | Expensive, but PCWorld listed it as $1,650 off; only worth it if you need high-end gaming/content-creation power. ([pcworld.com](https://www.pcworld.com/article/3145503/best-memorial-day-laptop-deals.html)) |

## My quick recommendation

- **Under $700:** Get the **Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5** deal at ~$600 if specs match your needs.
- **Best overall for most people:** **MacBook Air M5 13" with 16GB RAM / 512GB SSD** around **$949**.
- **Gaming:** Wait for Prime Day unless you need it now; gaming laptop prices often drop hard during major sale events.
- **Avoid unless desperate:** Very cheap off-brand laptops with older Pentium/Celeron chips, even if they advertise lots of RAM. DealNews showed a $299 laptop with 32GB RAM and 512GB SSD, but the Pentium Gold 6500Y CPU is old/low-power, so I’d only buy it for very basic web/email use. ([dealnews.com](https://www.dealnews.com/c49/Computers/Laptops/))

**Best move:** If you can wait until **June 23–26, 2026**, set price alerts now and compare Prime Day laptop prices against Best Buy, Lenovo, Dell, and Costco before buying.
